Red will paint an image where someone close to the person who activated it is depicted doing something (anything can be pictured), and the Foundation does not want anybody to know what the blue button does, since it does something so veil-breaking.

Okay, but as the author, you should know what the blue button does. This also feels a bit weird considering they would have had to have tested the blue button before to know what it does. We would know what the blue button does by the end of the story?

The story will be carried through an incident report, an interview log, testing logs, and addenda. The addenda will show how much the Foundation tried to keep the item secret, and prohibit any activation of the blue button. They started to implement procedures to try and keep it from being abused, and then after they did that, they opened it up again, but they still need to keep the blue button as a last resort.

This is a bare bones story. What would happen to make them need to use the button? Is there any particular reason they can't just shove it in the basement of site whatever and nobody would ever need to know what the blue button does until the researches dig it up.

final notes:

I feel this could be interesting, but right now it feels a little flat. Your base story isn't really engaging beyond needing to keep this SCP a secret with no real telling of the consequences of what would happen. You have a core anomaly which does a thing, but it won't be able to carry the narrative on its own.

Good luck!

item.title: [Seeking Greenlights] Big Red Button
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout w/ ACS, lots of addenda to expand on the concept, short testing logs and an incident report.

Elevator Pitch: It has the appearance of an ATM machine, with a glass front screen and 2 buttons on the ATM's base where the keypad normally is; the left button is red, and the right button is blue. The card reader slot on a normal ATM machine is used to insert a piece of paper/papyrus, and then a button can be pressed. Red will paint an image where someone close to the person who activated it is depicted doing something (anything can be pictured), and the Foundation does not want anybody to know what the blue button does, since it does something so veil-breaking.

Central Narrative: The story will be carried through an incident report, an interview log, testing logs, and addenda. The addenda will show how much the Foundation tried to keep the item secret, and prohibit any activation of the blue button. They started to implement procedures to try and keep it from being abused, and then after they did that, they opened it up again, but they still need to keep the blue button as a last resort.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story will be carried in-depth, and the mystery of what the second button will do and why it's so important to keep it even though it will be veil-breaking.

Additional Notes: This idea has been in my head for a while, and I just wanted to get it out there.
